text: Introduce students to fundamental programming concepts using Python. Topics include variables, data types, control flow (conditionals and loops), functions, recursion, file I/O, and basic data structures (lists, tuples, dictionaries). Lab component covers hands-on programming exercises.
Unit 1: Introduction to Python - variables, expressions, statements.
Unit 2: Control flow - if-else, while, for loops.
Unit 3: Functions - definition, arguments, return values, recursion.
Unit 4: Data structures - lists, tuples, sets, dictionaries.
Unit 5: File handling and exceptions.
Unit 6: Introduction to object-oriented programming.

Develop understanding of single and multivariable calculus with engineering and data science applications. Topics include limits, derivatives, integrals, sequences, series, and partial differentiation.
Unit 1: Functions, limits and continuity.
Unit 2: Differentiation - rules, chain rule, implicit differentiation, L'Hopital's rule.
Unit 3: Integration - indefinite and definite integrals, fundamental theorem of calculus, techniques of integration.
Unit 4: Sequences and series - convergence, Taylor and Maclaurin series.
Unit 5: Multivariable calculus - partial derivatives, gradient, chain rule, maxima and minima.
Introduce classical mechanics, waves, and special theory of relativity. Develop problem-solving skills in physics relevant to engineering applications.
Unit 1: Vectors, laws of motion, work and energy.
Unit 2: Rotational motion, angular momentum.
Unit 3: Oscillations - simple harmonic motion, damped and forced oscillations.
Unit 4: Waves - wave equation, superposition, standing waves, Doppler effect.
Unit 5: Special theory of relativity - Lorentz transformation, time dilation, mass-energy equivalence.
Understand fundamental data structures and algorithm design and analysis. Topics include arrays, linked lists, stacks, queues, trees, heaps, graphs, sorting, searching, and algorithm complexity.
Unit 1: Algorithm analysis - Big-O notation, recurrences, master theorem.
Unit 2: Linear data structures - arrays, linked lists, stacks, queues.
Unit 3: Trees - binary trees, BST, AVL trees, B-trees, heaps.
Unit 4: Graph algorithms - BFS, DFS, shortest paths (Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford), MST (Kruskal, Prim).
Unit 5: Sorting and searching - merge sort, quick sort, heap sort, binary search.
Unit 6: Dynamic programming and greedy algorithms.

Develop proficiency in linear algebra concepts essential for data science and machine learning. Topics include vector spaces, linear transformations, matrix decompositions, eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
Unit 1: Vectors and matrices - operations, row reduction, echelon form.
Unit 2: Vector spaces - subspaces, basis, dimension, rank.
Unit 3: Linear transformations - kernel, image, matrix representation.
Unit 4: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors - characteristic polynomial, diagonalisation.
Unit 5: Inner product spaces - orthogonality, Gram-Schmidt process.
Unit 6: Singular value decomposition (SVD) and applications.

Provide rigorous treatment of probability theory and statistical inference for data science applications. Topics include probability spaces, random variables, common distributions, estimation, hypothesis testing.
Unit 1: Probability spaces - sample space, events, axioms, conditional probability, Bayes' theorem.
Unit 2: Random variables - discrete and continuous distributions (Bernoulli, Binomial, Poisson, Uniform, Exponential, Normal).
Unit 3: Joint distributions, marginal and conditional distributions, independence.
Unit 4: Expectation, variance, covariance, moment generating functions.
Unit 5: Law of large numbers and central limit theorem.
Unit 6: Statistical inference - point and interval estimation, hypothesis testing, p-values.
Understand database system design, SQL, relational algebra, normalisation, transaction management and indexing. Students will design, implement and query relational databases.
Unit 1: Introduction - data models, database architecture, three-schema architecture.
Unit 2: Relational model - relational algebra and calculus, SQL DDL and DML.
Unit 3: Database design - ER modelling, normalisation (1NF, 2NF, 3NF, BCNF).
Unit 4: Indexing and hashing - B+ trees, hash indexes.
Unit 5: Query processing and optimisation.
Unit 6: Transaction management - ACID properties, concurrency control, recovery.

Introduce the foundational concepts, algorithms and applications of machine learning. Students will implement supervised, unsupervised and basic reinforcement learning algorithms and evaluate their performance.
Unit 1: ML fundamentals - supervised vs unsupervised learning, bias-variance tradeoff, overfitting.
Unit 2: Linear models - linear regression, logistic regression, regularisation (Ridge, LASSO).
Unit 3: Classification - k-NN, decision trees, random forests, SVM.
Unit 4: Unsupervised learning - k-means clustering, hierarchical clustering, PCA.
Unit 5: Model evaluation - cross-validation, ROC curves, confusion matrix, performance metrics.
Unit 6: Neural network basics - perceptron, multi-layer networks, backpropagation.
Understand data preprocessing, data warehouse design, OLAP, association rule mining, classification, clustering, and anomaly detection applied to large datasets.
Unit 1: Data preprocessing - cleaning, integration, transformation, reduction.
Unit 2: Data warehouse - architecture, OLAP, star and snowflake schemas.
Unit 3: Frequent pattern mining - Apriori algorithm, FP-growth, association rules.
Unit 4: Classification methods - Naive Bayes, decision trees applied to mining.
Unit 5: Clustering - DBSCAN, expectation-maximisation.
Unit 6: Anomaly detection and advanced topics.

Provide in-depth understanding of deep learning architectures including CNNs, RNNs, LSTMs, attention mechanisms, and transformers. Students will implement and train deep neural networks for real-world tasks.
Unit 1: Review of neural networks, backpropagation, optimisation (SGD, Adam).
Unit 2: Convolutional Neural Networks - architecture, pooling, training, transfer learning.
Unit 3: Recurrent Neural Networks - vanilla RNN, LSTM, GRU, sequence modelling.
Unit 4: Attention mechanisms and Transformers - self-attention, multi-head attention, BERT basics.
Unit 5: Generative models - VAEs, GANs.
Unit 6: Practical deep learning - regularisation, batch normalisation, hyperparameter tuning.

Introduce the theory and practice of natural language processing. Topics include text preprocessing, language models, word embeddings, sequence labelling, parsing, sentiment analysis, machine translation, and question answering.
Unit 1: Text preprocessing - tokenisation, stemming, lemmatisation, POS tagging, NER.
Unit 2: Language models - n-gram models, perplexity, neural language models.
Unit 3: Word representations - word2vec, GloVe, contextual embeddings (BERT).
Unit 4: Sequence modelling for NLP - CRFs, RNNs for sequence labelling.
Unit 5: Syntactic parsing - dependency parsing, constituency parsing.
Unit 6: Downstream tasks - sentiment analysis, machine translation, question answering.
Cover fundamentals of computer vision including image formation, feature extraction, object detection, image segmentation, and 3D vision. Hands-on implementation using deep learning frameworks.
Unit 1: Image formation - cameras, optics, geometric transformations.
Unit 2: Image processing - filtering, edge detection (Sobel, Canny), morphology.
Unit 3: Feature extraction - SIFT, HOG, deep features.
Unit 4: Object detection - sliding windows, R-CNN, YOLO, SSD.
Unit 5: Image segmentation - semantic and instance segmentation (Mask R-CNN, U-Net).
Unit 6: 3D vision - stereo vision, depth estimation, point clouds.
Understand operating system concepts including process management, memory management, file systems, and I/O. Relevant to data pipeline engineering and high-performance computing in data science.
Unit 1: Introduction - OS structure, system calls, processes.
Unit 2: Process management - scheduling algorithms, synchronisation, deadlock.
Unit 3: Memory management - paging, segmentation, virtual memory.
Unit 4: File systems - file organisation, directory structure, disk scheduling.
Unit 5: I/O systems and storage.
Unit 6: Security and protection.

Introduce the theory and algorithms of reinforcement learning. Topics include Markov decision processes, dynamic programming, Monte Carlo methods, temporal-difference learning, policy gradient methods, and deep RL.
Unit 1: Markov decision processes - states, actions, rewards, policies, value functions.
Unit 2: Dynamic programming - policy evaluation, policy improvement, value iteration.
Unit 3: Monte Carlo methods - prediction and control.
Unit 4: Temporal-difference learning - TD(0), SARSA, Q-learning.
Unit 5: Function approximation - linear approximation, neural network Q-learning (DQN).
Unit 6: Policy gradient methods - REINFORCE, actor-critic, PPO.
Learn scalable data processing frameworks and techniques for big data analytics. Topics include Hadoop ecosystem, Apache Spark, stream processing, NoSQL databases, and distributed machine learning.
Unit 1: Big data concepts - 3Vs (volume, velocity, variety), Hadoop ecosystem (HDFS, MapReduce).
Unit 2: Apache Spark - RDDs, DataFrames, Spark SQL, MLlib.
Unit 3: Stream processing - Apache Kafka, Spark Streaming, Flink concepts.
Unit 4: NoSQL databases - key-value, document, column-family, graph databases.
Unit 5: Distributed machine learning - parameter servers, federated learning concepts.
Unit 6: Case studies and project.

Cover classical and modern optimisation methods used in machine learning and operations research. Topics include convex optimisation, linear programming, gradient-based methods, constrained optimisation.
Unit 1: Convexity - convex sets and functions, optimality conditions.
Unit 2: Linear programming - simplex method, duality.
Unit 3: Unconstrained optimisation - gradient descent, Newton's method, quasi-Newton methods.
Unit 4: Constrained optimisation - Lagrangian multipliers, KKT conditions.
Unit 5: Stochastic optimisation - SGD, Adam, momentum methods.
Unit 6: Applications in machine learning.

Understand computer networking fundamentals relevant to distributed data systems and cloud computing. Topics include layered network architecture, TCP/IP, routing, DNS, HTTP, and network security basics.
Unit 1: Introduction - network architecture, OSI and TCP/IP models.
Unit 2: Application layer - HTTP, DNS, SMTP, P2P.
Unit 3: Transport layer - TCP, UDP, flow control, congestion control.
Unit 4: Network layer - IP addressing, routing algorithms (OSPF, BGP).
Unit 5: Link layer - Ethernet, MAC, ARP.
Unit 6: Network security basics.

Address ethical dimensions of AI and data science including algorithmic bias, fairness, transparency, accountability, privacy, and societal impact. Students will analyse case studies and develop frameworks for responsible AI.
Unit 1: AI ethics landscape - key principles, stakeholders, regulatory context.
Unit 2: Algorithmic bias - sources, measurement, mitigation.
Unit 3: Fairness - definitions (demographic parity, equalised odds), trade-offs.
Unit 4: Explainability and interpretability - LIME, SHAP, model cards.
Unit 5: Privacy - differential privacy, federated learning, data governance.
Unit 6: Societal impact, policy, and professional responsibility.

Students undertake a substantial research or applied project integrating skills from across the DSAI programme. Projects may involve real-world data, novel models, or deployment of ML systems. Students work under faculty supervision and present their findings.
Unit 1: Project definition and literature review.
Unit 2: Data collection and preprocessing.
Unit 3: Model design and development.
Unit 4: Experimentation, evaluation, and iteration.
Unit 5: Technical writing and report preparation.
Unit 6: Final presentation and demonstration.
A student shall not register for more than 26 credits in any semester during the first two years (Semesters 1–4), unless granted explicit permission by the Dean (Academics).
A student shall not register for fewer than 12 credits in any regular semester, except in the final semester or under medical/special circumstances approved by the Dean (Academics).

text: Eligibility criteria for a Minor programme at IIT Bhilai require completion of a specified number of additional elective courses (typically 5 courses / 20 credits) in the chosen discipline beyond the student's major programme requirements.

filter_metadata.applies_to: B.Tech all programmes seeking a Minor

text: UNRESOLVED: The minimum CGPA threshold (if any) required for a student to be eligible to pursue a Minor programme at IIT Bhilai could not be confirmed from publicly accessible official documents as of the retrieval date.
A student may not register for a course unless all hard prerequisites listed in the official curriculum for that course have been completed with a passing grade.

In the event that a student has not completed a prerequisite course due to exceptional circumstances (such as a medical leave), the student may apply to the Department Academic Committee (DAC) for a prerequisite waiver.
Course registration is done online through the academic portal during the designated registration window announced by the Academic Office. Late registration attracts a penalty fee.

IIT Bhilai permits students to earn academic credit by completing NPTEL/SWAYAM courses, subject to prior approval from the Department Academic Committee (DAC) and the Academic Office. The number of credits transferable is determined by the credit equivalence policy.

A student who completes a NPTEL/SWAYAM course with a minimum score as specified by the NPTEL portal (typically ≥ 40% in the proctored exam) and submits the certificate to the Academic Office within the specified deadline is eligible for credit transfer consideration.

filter_metadata.applies_to: B.Tech all programmes seeking NPTEL credit transfer

text: NPTEL/SWAYAM credits earned and transferred to the academic record may be counted towards elective credit requirements of the B.Tech programme, but generally may not substitute for core programme courses without special approval.
IIT Bhilai follows a 10-point grading scale. The passing grade in a course is D (5 grade points). A student obtaining F (0 grade points) has failed the course and must repeat it.
A student will normally not be allowed to register and program will be auto terminated if (i) his/her CGPA falls below 4.0 (ii) his/her CGPA falls below 4.5 for three consecutive semesters.
